title: Why You Blame Others When Things Go Wrong
hook: Ever notice how your successes are always your fault?

narration.text: When we succeed, we often attribute it to our own skills and efforts.
But when we fail, we tend to blame external circumstances.
This cognitive bias is called the self-serving bias.
Our brains protect our self-esteem by taking credit for good outcomes.
It also deflects responsibility for negative ones.
Recognising this bias helps us understand our reactions better.
It encourages a more balanced view of events.
Have you noticed this pattern in your own thoughts?

description: Discover the self-serving bias, a common cognitive trick our minds play. Learn why we take credit for success and blame external factors for failure, and how this impacts our daily lives.
topic: Why people tend to attribute success to their own skill and failure to external factors.
